blindSummary:
This state/province is the clearest case in the country of a sub-national government reversing course on trans rights within one election cycle. A 2020 education policy protected 2SLGBTQIA+ student privacy and inclusion. In July 2023, the government then in office amended it to require parental consent for under-16 name/pronoun use, triggering protests outside the legislature. The successor government reversed the amendment on 19 December 2024, effective 1 January 2025: parental consent is now "encouraged but no longer required" for the informal use of chosen names and pronouns by students of any age (it remains required for formal use in official records for students under 16), with a "presumed capacity" concept based on the child-and-youth advocate's recommendations. The revised policy text extends its application to the whole school environment, including "visiting professionals, student teachers, parents, volunteers, and visitors", so current school rules technically reach non-residents present in classrooms.

The reversal is a strong positive institutional response - a government that legislated against trans students repealed the provision after one term. The residual signal is the demonstrated capacity for hostile policy within an election cycle and the 2023 protest period, which leave a slightly higher baseline of political volatility than jurisdictions that never legislated against trans people. No street-level disruption of public expression events was documented. The current effective policy is protective, and a further reversal would move the position again.
